analysis.title: US Market Intelligence | Afternoon Briefing (October 27, 2026)
key_insights: US stocks closed higher led by tech: SPX +0.6%, NDX +1.3%, RTY +1.2%. Breadth was weaker than the headline, with the equal-weight S&P (SPW) lagging SPX by about 60bp.
The AI trade had another strong session ahead of Mag 7 earnings (GOOGL and MSFT Wednesday, AMZN Thursday), led by semis/memory, neoclouds and networking. TSLA, GOOGL and AMZN led the Mag 7.

JPM trader Brian Heavey says the AI picks-and-shovels trade is clearing some, not all, of the hurdles to another leg higher. Financing pressure eased after META raised $97.5B (with $60B to be deployed via ATM from January), a $40B SPCX GPU equipment deal, and a $63B AVGO SPV for custom chips.
Heavey sees evidence of re-risking but calls it tentative, with light volumes. He says semis and optical are better to buy here, and the info tech buy-side flow is about 1.25x to 1 buy-heavy.
Heavey reports GOOG is being used as a source of funds, with another negative third-party check ahead of earnings that points to a Search miss.

Earnings macro read-through: AI infrastructure demand is still accelerating (Corning, Hubbell data center sales +80% organic, Nucor, UPS sizing data center logistics at $15B), while energy and freight costs are spreading as an inflation source.
Freeport-McMoRan said diesel costs have more than doubled this year and US electricity rates rose significantly between Q2 and Q3. Coca-Cola cited elevated logistics and transportation costs.
Xylem said utility projects are slowing because contractors are tied up on AI jobs, suggesting the AI buildout could raise specialized labor costs in the short to medium term.

UPS (+6%) raised its outlook on restructuring and higher-paying shipments. KO (-2%) lifted its annual target but North America volumes were flat. BA fell 11% on a wider-than-expected jet unit loss and stalled deliveries.
Oct consumer confidence jumped to 91.7 vs 81.0 survey. The 5Y auction tailed 0.4bp and 2Y yields rose 1bp. WTI fell 1.8% to just under $100.

FOMC preview (Feroli): he expects a hold this week with two hawkish dissents from Hammack and Logan, and a risk that Kashkari also dissents. He expects the statement to say policy will deliver a timely return to price stability.

Feroli says Chair Warsh must explain why the committee hiked after a two-tenths core PCE print in September but is now holding ahead of an expected three-tenths outturn. He suggests the Committee is biased to hike but wants more time to see the effect of last month's hike.

JPM US Market Intel expects Fed-induced volatility could extend into the following week, with focus on how policymakers reassess the December meeting and 2027 path after the hawkish September inflation print, and on emerging AI concerns.

JPM remains Tactically Bullish. SPX is down 2.4% over two weeks and -36bp MTD. The case rests on flash PMIs pointing to roughly 5% annualized real growth for a second month and Q3 earnings tracking the pre-season forecast (about 13% revenue growth, 30% EPS growth, 15% margins).
JPM notes sentiment is firmly in Fear but a full positioning washout has not occurred, so the signal is less clear.
Last week the Recession L/S basket returned 3.4% and the Stagflation L/S basket 1.5%, even though 1Y and 2Y inflation breakevens and bond yields fell. Oil rose for the 4th straight week.

Iran is a key risk: Trump is nearing a decision between negotiation and continued attacks, with a third aircraft carrier approaching. If he returns to negotiation, JPM expects a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy.

Updated Monetization Menu: add hedges via longs in oil/Energy equities and long vol. The Oct 19 menu favored Tech, pairs trades and derivatives for a rebound, with constructive views on Financials and Retailers, and Brazil and Japan internationally.
Europe: European semis rallied over 5% (a 1.5z move). UKX -0.8%, SX5E +0.8%, SXXP +0.5%, DAX +0.7%.
Midterms: JPM cites Nate Silver's analysis that polls did not underestimate Republicans in 2018 or 2022 (average error 0 points in 2018, Democrats underestimated by 0.3 in 2022).

earnings_insights: UPS (reported 10/27): raised its sales and profit outlook on restructuring traction and higher-paying shipments, stock +6%. It put the data center logistics opportunity at $15B.
Coca-Cola KO (reported 10/27): lifted its annual profit target, stock -2%, with flat North America volumes and elevated logistics and transportation cost pressure.
Boeing BA (reported 10/27): wider-than-expected jet unit loss and stalled deliveries, stock -11%. The company is not yet stably producing wings for a 47-a-month rate.
Hubbell HUBB (reported 10/27): data center sales rose over 80% organically.
Freeport-McMoRan FCX (reported 10/27): diesel was the biggest cost factor, more than doubling this year, and US electricity rates rose significantly from Q2 to Q3.
Nucor NUE (reported 10/27): Section 232 measures are helping it capture more demand, with finished steel imports down more than 13% y/y and 24% vs 2024.
Q3 S&P 500 earnings season, about a quarter reported: no dips so far versus the pre-season forecast of roughly 13% revenue growth, 30% EPS growth and 15% margins (JPM).
Earnings due 10/28: GOOGL and MSFT after the close, among others. AMZN reports 10/29.

tension_points.bull_case: Fed holds this week and signals it wants more time to see the effect of last month's hike, which limits further tightening risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Two hawkish dissents (Hammack, Logan) and possibly Kashkari, a bias to hike, and an expected three-tenths core PCE print keep the path hawkish and may extend Fed-induced volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed statement or press conference that conveys no bias to hike, or a core PCE print on Oct 29 below the expected three-tenths.

tension_points.bull_case: Financing hurdles are clearing (META, SPCX, AVGO deals and the S-1 timing on track), with semis, optical and hardware leading.
tension_points.bear_case: Re-risking is tentative, volumes are light, breadth is weak, and Mag 7 earnings this week are a hurdle, including a possible GOOG Search miss.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Mag 7 earnings disappointment this week or renewed financing pressure.

tension_points.what_invalidates: Trump choosing continued attacks on Iran over negotiation.
